**Full attention stores access to individual past tokens; a recurrent state compresses the past.** In full attention, the current query can compare with each earlier key. A state-space model instead updates a fixed-size state as tokens arrive. Linear-attention constructions can also accumulate suitable summaries so a new query uses stored statistics rather than revisiting a full token-by-token score matrix. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.00752) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.21060)

**A running-summary analogy.** To compute a running average, you need only a count and sum, not every previous number. A recurrent model learns a much richer summary, but the basic tradeoff remains: compact state saves memory while potentially discarding details needed by future questions.

For fixed state width, each new token updates a bounded amount of state, making recurrent-state memory independent of sequence length. Training can exploit scans or structured/chunked matrix operations, giving linear scaling in length under the architecture's fixed-size assumptions. Constants and parallel efficiency still matter.

**Why exact retrieval can be hard.** Suppose a long context contains thousands of arbitrary key–value pairs, and only at the end do you learn which key will be queried. A compact state must preserve enough information about many possible answers in advance. Full attention retains explicit token-level access, giving it a different capability–memory tradeoff.

“O(1) memory per step” refers to recurrent sequence state, not all model weights, training activations, or arbitrary output storage. Hybrid models add attention layers to recover some explicit retrieval ability. Evaluate the actual tasks and lengths; asymptotic efficiency alone does not determine which architecture gives the best quality at a fixed serving budget.

**Technical details and references.**

A state-space layer updates a fixed-size state, while kernelized linear attention accumulates sufficient statistics. For fixed feature/state dimension, both avoid an explicit sequence-by-sequence score matrix. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.00752) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.21060)

$$h_t=A_th_{t-1}+B_tx_t,\qquad S_t=S_{t-1}+\phi(k_t)v_t^T,\quad z_t=z_{t-1}+\phi(k_t),\quad y_t=\frac{\phi(q_t)^TS_t}{\phi(q_t)^Tz_t}.$$

The linear-attention state costs $O(rd_v+r)$, independent of sequence length but not of model width. Associative scans or chunked algorithms permit parallel training; autoregressive inference updates the state once per token. Compression can discard distinctions needed for exact retrieval of arbitrary old items. Full attention retains token-level keys/values and offers direct content-addressable access. “Linear” assumes fixed state dimensions and does not make every practical implementation faster at short lengths.
